subject: headcrab
leg: control: Valve's own against the brief
label: headcrab.mdl, in the place of the game's models/headcrab.mdl

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/chumtoad.mdl, models/roach.mdl, models/leech.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 3 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked D, A, B where the asset was C, C, C: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: Against the brief's words, the silhouette reads as a low, flattened headcrab-like body on four legs. In the left and right views the cream dome sits over the legs, the front claws reach forward and down, and the rear legs meet the body. The top view shows the splayed legs the brief implies, with no part sticking out wrongly.

M2.reason: Measured 25.9 long and 13.2 high against the brief's 26 and 13, both well inside 15%. Width is 19.2, which the brief does not give, so it is not scored against anything.

M3.reason: Parts the brief asks for, checked down to the small ones: a cream shell over the legs (cream dome in the left, right and front views); two sharp red front claws (red, pointed, at the front in the left, front and top views); a mouth underneath (toothed maw in the below view). Four legs are present: red front claws and brown rear legs with dark tips (back and back-left views). Nothing the brief names is missing. The mouth is a toothed round opening rather than a true beak, but it sits where the brief puts it.

M4.reason: The red front claws match the brief. The shell does not read as cream-coloured: the cream covers only the top dome and the centre, while the rim and sides of the shell are brown and ridged (left, right and back views). The brief's cream shell is only partly there.

M5.reason: The brief names no markings. The shell carries fine ridges and a veined texture, the mouth has teeth detail, and the claw tips are dark. Nothing is added that the brief rules out.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the rubric for this kind. The line-up test ran three times and the judges picked the wrong one each time (D, A, B where the asset was C), so the test does not separate it from the game's own. The picture also does not show plainly which of A to D is the asset, and that is not settled here.

M7.reason: The front is where the brief puts it: the red claws and the mouth are at the front and underside, and the body stands upright on its legs with the claw tips on the ground line in the left and right views. No origin measure was given, so standing on its origin is judged by eye only.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors. Triangles are 478, under twice the Half-Life median of 308 (616) and under the third quartile (340), so they pass the amended bar for props. Nothing visible is open, inside out or floating in the side, top, below or angle views.
